notes.text: Kingdom/City: Kingdom of Saba (Sheba); Approximate Duration: Existed before birth of Hazrat Esa A.S; Notable Events and Features: Renowned for advanced irrigation systems, including the Marib Dam; a wealthy trading nation.

Kingdom/City: Himyarite Kingdom; Approximate Duration: 115 BC- 525 AD; Notable Events and Features: Succeeded the Sabaeans; Mostly it was Christian and Judist state.Its known for adopting Judaism in the 4th century CE.
Kingdom/City: Abraha; Approximate Duration: Conquered Himyars in 525 AD; Notable Events and Features: Ruler of Abyssinia

Kingdom/City: Year of the Elephant; Approximate Duration: Circa 570 CE; Notable Events and Features: Abraha, a Christian ruler from Yemen, attempted to attack Mecca with an army that included elephants; his plan failed due to divine intervention. His lead elephant, named Mahmud, halted and refused to advance. His expedition was then attacked by Ababeels.

Mecca - Arid, water-scarce region (no agriculture or natural rivers).; Known as a major trade hub due to its location on caravan routes.; Governed by tribal aristocracy - Al-Mala (Council of Elders).; Kaaba was the religious center, housing 360 idols of different tribes.; Religious practices were polytheistic with no firm belief in afterlife or resurrection.; Each tribe had a deity, and each deity was daughter of Supreme God.; Controlled by the Quraysh tribe, who gained dominance through:; Custodianship of Kaaba; Ilaf trade pacts ensuring secure trade routes; Organizing major trade caravans (e.g., to Yemen and Syria).; Annual pilgrimage brought economic and political clout.; Social system was tribal with strong kinship bonds. System of Collective Responsibility was present.

Medina - A fertile oasis region, suitable for agriculture.; Inhabited by two main Arab tribes: Aws and Khazraj.; Also home to several Jewish tribes: Banu Qaynuqa, Banu Nadir, Banu Qurayza.; Politically fragmented - frequent tribal conflicts and civil wars.; Later became the first Islamic state and center for spreading Islam.
Hilf-ul-Fudool - Pact to support oppressed and uphold justice.; Formed in Mecca (~591 CE) before Prophethood.; Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم actively participated.
Black Stone Incident - Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم called Al-Amin (The Trustworthy) by Quraysh.; Resolved Black Stone dispute during Kaaba reconstruction (~605 CE).
Social Boycott - Duration: 616-619 CE,3 years in Shi'b Abi Talib.; Imposed by Quraysh against Banu Hashim and Muslims.; Severe hardship, starvation, and isolation.
First Migration to Abyssinia - Year: 615 CE.; 11 men,4 women migrated.; Led by Hazrat Uthman ibn Mazʽun; Protected by King Najashi (Negus).
Second Migration to Abyssinia - Year: 616 CE.; 83 men,18 women migrated.; Led by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (RA).; Quraysh delegation failed to bring them back.
Journey to Taif - Year: 619 CE; Sought support in Taif, was rejected and attacked.; Comforted by Addas, a Christian slave.
Amm ul Hazan (Year of Sorrow). - Year: 619 CE (10 Nabvi); Wife Hazrat Khadija R.A and Uncle Abu Talib R.A passed away.

First Pledge of Al- Aqabah - Year: 621 CE.; 12 men from Medina (Yathrib) accepted Islam.; Pledged moral obedience and faithfulness.; Hazrat Musab R.A was sent as representative to Medina.(First Ambassador of Islam)
Second Pledge of Al- Aqabah - Year: 622 CE.; 73 men,2 women pledged full support including military help.

Battle of Bu'ath (617 AD) - Tribal war between Aws and Khazraj (Arab Tribes) in Medina.; 3 Jewish tribes (Qaynuqa, Nadir, Qurayza) also took part in war.; Occurred just before Hijrah.; Created a power vacuum; led people to seek Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم's leadership.
Hijrah (Migration to Medina) - Year: 622 CE.; Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم migrated from Mecca to Medina.; Details (with bullets): Start of Islamic calendar (Hijri).; Warm welcome by Ansar.

Mithaq-e-Madina (Constitution of Medina) - Year: 622 CE (1 AH); Between muslims and 8 Arab Tribes and some Jewish Tribes; Mawakhawat (Each Muhajir was made brother to a Ansar) (e.g, Abu Ayyub al-Ansari became brother to Prophet SAW); Total 47 articles.; Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم was declared head of state.; Ensured unity, mutual defense, and religious freedom.

Kutbah Hajj tul Widah - Hajj-ul-Wida was performed in: 10 AH / 632 AD; Location of the farewell sermon: Mount Arafat; Total number of companions in Hajj-ul-Wida: Approx. 1,20,000 - 1,44,000; Total Hajj performed by Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم: One; Other name of Hajj-ul-Wida: Farewell Pilgrimage; Day of Khutba-e-Hajjatul Wida: 9th Dhul-Hijjah; Interest declared void starting from: Prophet's uncle Abbas (starting with the interest of his uncle Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib.); Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم declared: No Prophet will come after me; Collective responsibility of murder (blood revenge) - starting with the blood money of Ibn Rabiah

Name: Battle of Badr; Year (CE/AH): 2 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Quraysh opposed Islam; caravan conflict; Happened on 17 Ramzan; Muslim strength: 313; Quraish strength: Around 1000; Muslim martyrs: 14; Quraish killed: 70; Quraish captured: 70; Abu Jahl was injured by Mu'adh and Maud; Abu Jahl was killed by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA); Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): Abu Jahl (Amr ibn Hisham)
First Muslim martyr: Mihja' (RA); Other Quraish leaders killed: Utbah bin Rabi'ah, Shaybah bin Rabi'ah, Walid bin Utbah

Name: Battle of Uhud; Year (CE/AH): 3 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Muslim strength: Initially 1000, reduced to 700; Abdullah bin Ubayy (chief hypocrite / Munafkeen) deserted with 300 men before battle; Quraish strength: 3000; Reason: Quraish revenge for defeat at Badr; 50 archers were stationed on a hill by Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم with strict orders not to leave; Khalid bin Walid attacked from behind with cavalry; Muslim martyrs: 70; Key martyr: Hazrat Hamza (RA) - killed by Wahshi ibn Harb (hired by Hind wife of Abu Saufyan); Two teeth of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم were broken; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): Abu Sufyan ibn Harb

Name: Battle of the Trench (Ahzab); Year (CE/AH): 5 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Year: 5 AH / 627 AD; Muslim strength: Around 3000; Enemy strength: 10,000 (combined Quraish + Jewish tribes + other Arab tribes); Salman Farsi (RA) suggested digging a trench (Khandaq) around Madinah; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): Abu Sufyan ibn Harb (Quraysh-led coalition)

Jewish tribe Banu Qurayzah broke treaty and betrayed Muslims during siege; After battle, they were punished as per Jewish law by decision of Sa'ad bin Mu'az (RA); Known as Battle of Ahzab (Ahzab means Coalition/Allies); Quran mentions this in Surah Al-Ahzab (33); Demolished Masjid-e- Zarar after war.

Name: Sulah-e- Hudaibiyah (Bayt e Rizwan); Year (CE/AH): 6 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Rumors of death of Hazrat Usman RA led to Bayt e Rizwan; Treaty between Muslims & Quraysh after blocked Umrah attempt; Muslim strength: 1400; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): Suhail ibn Amr (Quraysh negotiator)

Name: Battle of Khaybar; Year (CE/AH): 7 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Main tribe involved: Banu Nadir (expelled earlier from Madinah, regrouped at Khyber); Other Jewish tribes in Khyber: Banu Quraizah, Banu Qainuqa; Key Muslim warrior in Khyber: Hazrat Ali (RA) - famously broke the fort door as a shield.; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): Marhab

Name: Conquest of Makkah; Year (CE/AH): 8 AH (630 CE); Cause / Significance/Important Information: Quraysh violated treaty; Makkah taken without battle; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): Abu Sufyan (submitted to Islam)

Name: Battle of Hunayn; Year (CE/AH): 8 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Tribes (Hawazin/Thaqif) resisted growing Muslim power >Result: Muslims initially retreated but gained decisive victory; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم

Name: Battle of Tabuk; Year (CE/AH): 9 AH; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Anticipated Byzantine threat >Result: No actual battle; Byzantines retreated without engagement; Led by (Muslims): Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Led by (Opponents): No direct battle; Byzantine army withdrew

Name: Ridda Wars (Apostasy Wars); Year (CE/AH): 632-633 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Tribal rebellion after Prophet's death; Led by (Muslims): Caliph Abu Bakr (RA); Led by (Opponents): Musaylimah, Tulayha, Sajjah, others

Name: Battle of Yamama (part of Ridda Wars); Year (CE/AH): 633 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Fierce battle against false prophet Musaylimah >Result: Muslims won; heavy casualties,70 Huffaz martyred; Led by (Muslims): Khalid ibn al- Walid (RA); Led by (Opponents): Musaylimah (killed)

Name: Battle of Yarmouk; Year (CE/AH): 636 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Byzantine resistance to Islamic expansion >Result: Major Byzantine defeat; opened Syria to Muslim rule >Got Palestine; Led by (Muslims): Khalid ibn al- Walid (RA); Led by (Opponents): Emperor Heraclius' army

Name: Battle of Qadisiyyah; Year (CE/AH): 636 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Persian resistance from Sassanid Empire > Result: Key victory; led to Muslim control of Iraq; Led by (Muslims): Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
Name: Battle of Nahavand; Year (CE/AH): 642 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Final Sassanid resistance >Result: Crushing Muslim victory; >Collapse of Sassanid Empire

Name: Conquest of Palestine / Jerusalem; Year (CE/AH): 637 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Jerusalem peacefully surrendered by Patriarch Sophronius; Led by (Muslims): Caliph Umar ibn al- Khattab (RA)

Name: Conquest of Egypt; Year (CE/AH): 640-642 CE; Cause / Significance/Important Information: Byzantine control challenged; Egypt brought under Islamic rule; Led by (Muslims): Amr ibn al- As (RA) (Fateh-e- Misar)
Tribe Name: Banu Qaynuqa; Year (AH): 2 AH; Cause / Significance: Insult and mistreatment of a Muslim woman by a goldsmith in market; Outcome / Result: Expelled from Madinah; migrated to Syria
Tribe Name: Banu Nadir; Year (AH): 4 AH; Cause / Significance: Planned assassination of Prophet; breach of treaty obligations; Outcome / Result: Expelled after siege; settled in Khaybar

Tribe Name: Banu Qurayza; Year (AH): 5 AH; Cause / Significance: Treason during Battle of Trench; allied with Quraysh against Muslims; Outcome / Result: Tribe besieged; men executed (as per Sa'd bin Mu'adh's verdict), women and children enslaved

Ruler / Caliph: Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم; Period (CE): 610-632 CE; Key Contributions / Events (Detailed): Established Islamic state in Medina (622 CE); Capital: Medina, State divided into 10 provinces including Madina (after Fatah e Mecca); Formation of Ashab-e-Suffah (students living in Masjid Nabwi); Ghanimah (war booty): 4/5 to soldiers,1/5 to Bayt-ul-Mal; Major battles: Badr (624), Uhud (625), Khandaq (627), Khyber (628), Hunayn (630) etc.

Ruler / Caliph: Abu Bakr Siddiq (RA); Period (CE): 632-634 CE; Key Contributions / Events (Detailed): Ridda Wars (Apostasy wars) against rebels & false prophets; Abu Bakr (RA) appointed Zaid bin Thabit (RA) to collect and compile the Quran.; 11 major expeditions led against rebels (Fitna Irtidad, Fitna Rad ul Zakat); Major false prophets: - Musailma al-Kadhdhab (Yamamah) - killed in Battle of Yamamah - Tulayha (Banu Asad, Najd) - later repented Sajah (Tamim) - later reverted - Aswad Ansi (Yemen) - killed by Fayruz; Conquests started: Entry into Syria and Iraq; Compilation of Qur'an initiated after many Hufaz were martyred in Yamamah

Ruler / Caliph: Umar ibn al- Khattab (RA); Period (CE): 634-644 CE; Key Contributions / Events (Detailed): Massive expansion: Persia, Egypt, Syria, Jerusalem conquered; Key battles: Battle of Qadisiyyah (636), Yarmouk (636), Nihawand (642); Administrative reforms: - Judicial system formalized (Chief Qadi: Ali RA) - Diwan (army register/payroll) created on suggestion of Hormizan - Police system established - Prison system (first prison was Safwan bin Umayyah's house) - Calendar started from Hijrah (16 AH) - Census conducted by Mukharma ibn Naufil - Added horses to zakat - Ushar (tax on merchandise) introduced - Canals built: Nahr Amir al-Momineen, Nahr Abu Musa - Conquests reached Sindh borders and Caucasus

Ruler / Caliph: Uthman ibn Affan (RA); Period (CE): 644-656 CE; Key Contributions / Events (Detailed): Compilation of Qur'an finalized (Mushaf Uthmani); Known as Jama Ul Quran; Standard copies sent to all provinces; Masjid Nabawi extension in 29 AH; Title Zul-Nurayn (Possessor of Two Lights) - married to Ruqayyah & Umm Kulthum (RA) daughters of Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم; Continued conquests: North Africa, Cyprus, Armenia; Naval campaigns expanded; Discontent due to governors led to martyrdom in 656 CE

Ruler / Caliph: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA); Period (CE): 656-661 CE; Key Contributions / Events (Detailed): Battles during reign: - Battle of Jamal (Camel) (656 CE) - Battle of Siffin (657 CE) - Battle of Nahrawan (658 CE); Shifted capital to Kufa; Known as "Arabian Nousherwan" (just administrator); Served as Chief Qadi during Umar's era; Killed by Kharijite Ibn Muljam (661 CE)

Name: Abu Bakr As-Siddiq (RA); Duration of Reign: 632-634 CE; Method of Selection/Election: Elected by consensus (Ijma') of Sahaba; Details of the Process: After the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)'s demise, there was a gathering at Saqifah Banu Sa'ida where Ansar proposed a leader. Umar (RA) pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr (RA), followed by others. He was chosen due to his close companionship with the Prophet and his leadership in prayers.

Name: Umar ibn Al- Khattab (RA); Duration of Reign: 634-644 CE; Method of Selection/Election: Appointed by Abu Bakr (RA); Details of the Process: On his deathbed, Abu Bakr (RA) consulted senior companions and then nominated Umar (RA) as his successor. The nomination was accepted by the majority of Sahaba.

Name: Uthman ibn Affan (RA); Duration of Reign: 644-656 CE; Method of Selection/Election: Selected by Shura (Consultative Council); Details of the Process: Umar (RA), before his death, formed a committee of six companions (Shura) to select the next caliph: Ali (RA), Uthman (RA), Zubair (RA), Talha (RA), Abdur Rahman bin Auf (RA), and Saad bin Abi Waqqas (RA). Abdur Rahman bin Auf (RA) took public opinion and declared Uthman (RA) as Caliph.

Name: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA); Duration of Reign: 656-661 CE; Method of Selection/Election: Elected by public pledge (Bay'ah); Details of the Process: After the martyrdom of Uthman (RA), there was public unrest. People, especially from Medina and Egypt, urged Ali (RA) to take leadership. He initially hesitated but later accepted when a majority of people gave Bay'ah.

Event: Assassination of Uthman (RA); Year (CE): 656 CE; Major Belligerents: Rebels from Egypt, Kufa, and Basra vs Caliph Uthman (RA); Causes: Complaints about provincial governors (especially Muawiyah in Syria and Abdullah ibn Saad in Egypt) - Accusations of nepotism (Umayyad relatives appointed) - Demand for reforms and replacement of governors -A forged letter incident (allegedly bearing Usman's seal) was intercepted by rebels. It ordered the killing of rebels - said to be authored or engineered by Marwan without Usman's knowledge. This deepened mistrust and triggered violence.; Outcome: Uthman (RA) was martyred after a siege of 40 days at his home in Medina. This sparked the First Fitna (civil war).

Event: Battle of the Camel (Jamal); Year (CE): 656 CE; Major Belligerents: Caliph Ali (RA) vs Aisha (RA), Talha (RA), Zubair (RA); Causes: Demand for revenge against Uthman's killers - Aisha (RA) and companions wanted justice before accepting Ali's rule -Miscommunication and manipulation by rebels worsened situation; Outcome: Ali (RA) won; Talha and Zubair were killed, Aisha (RA) was respectfully sent back to Medina. Conflict deepened within Ummah.

Event: Battle of Siffin; Year (CE): 657 CE; Major Belligerents: Caliph Ali (RA) vs Muawiyah (RA) (Governor of Syria); Causes: Muawiyah demanded justice for Uthman's murder before pledging allegiance to Ali (RA); Outcome: Battle ended in stalemate. Arbitration was proposed (Hakamiyat), leading to further divisions.

Event: Battle of Nahrawan; Year (CE): 658 CE; Major Belligerents: Caliph Ali (RA) vs Kharijites (former supporters of Ali); Causes: Kharijites rejected arbitration at Siffin - Declared both Ali and Muawiyah as illegitimate - Rebelled violently against Ali's rule; Outcome: Ali (RA) crushed the Kharijites, but their ideology persisted. Later, a Kharijite assassinated Ali in 661 CE.
Caliph: Abu Bakr As- Siddiq (RA); End of Reign / Removal: Natural death in 634 CE; Cause of End of Reign: Illness after 2 years of rule

Caliph: Umar ibn Al- Khattab (RA); End of Reign / Removal: Assassinated by a Persian slave Abu Lu'lu' Feroz (Slave of Mughira ibn Shu'ba); Cause of End of Reign: Stabbed in Fajr prayer; died three days later
Caliph: Uthman ibn Affan (RA); End of Reign / Removal: Assassinated by rebels in Medina; Cause of End of Reign: Rebels from Egypt, Kufa, and Basra besieged his house and killed him
Caliph: Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA); End of Reign / Removal: Assassinated by a Kharijite named Ibn Muljam; Cause of End of Reign: Attacked while going for Fajr prayer in Kufa

Ruler: Imam Hassan ibn Ali (RA); Reign Period: 661 - 661 CE (approx. 6 months); Notes: After Ali's martyrdom, Hassan (RA) became caliph. Later, he abdicated peacefully in favor of Muawiyah (RA) to avoid bloodshed - this is known as the Treaty of Hassan- Muawiyah.

Ruler: Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (RA); Reign Period: 661 - 680 CE; Notes: After Hassan's abdication, Muawiyah (RA) became first Umayyad Caliph. His rule brought relative stability. However, he nominated his son Yazid before his death, which later triggered the Second Fitna.

Phase/Event: Yazid's Succession; Period (CE / AH): 680 CE; Key Figures / Belligerents: Yazid ibn Muawiyah becomes Caliph; Causes: Violation of Hassan-Muawiyah treaty (Yazid's appointment was against agreed terms) - Many Sahaba refused allegiance to Yazid

Phase/Event: Battle of Karbala; Period (CE / AH): 680 CE / 10 Muharram 61 AH; Key Figures / Belligerents: Yazid's army vs Imam Hussain ibn Ali (RA); Causes: Hussain (RA) refused to pledge allegiance to Yazid - Invited by people of Kufa but betrayed - Martyred at Karbala; Outcome: Imam Hussain (RA) and family martyred; turning point in Islamic history; deepened Sunni-Shia split

Phase/Event: Abdullah ibn Zubair's Revolt (Son of Hazrat Zubair R.A); Period (CE / AH): 680 - 692 CE; Key Figures / Belligerents: Ibn Zubair vs Umayyads (Yazid, Marwan, Abdul Malik); Causes: Ibn Zubair declared himself Caliph in Makkah after Yazid's death - Controlled Hijaz, Iraq, parts of Levant; Outcome: Prolonged civil war; Ibn Zubair ruled as rival caliph

Phase/Event: Siege of Makkah (Kaaba burnt); Period (CE / AH): 683 CE; Key Figures / Belligerents: Yazid's army vs Ibn Zubair; Causes: Umayyads tried to crush Ibn Zubair's rebellion - Kaaba damaged during siege; Outcome: Siege ended after Yazid's sudden death; army retreated

Phase/Event: Marwan I and Abdul Malik's Reign; Period (CE / AH): 684 - 692 CE; Key Figures / Belligerents: Umayyad Caliphs fighting Ibn Zubair; Causes: Reassertion of Umayyad control over fragmented caliphate; Outcome: Abdul Malik defeated and killed Ibn Zubair in 692 CE; Umayyad rule restored

Phase/Event: End of Second Fitna; Period (CE / AH): 692 CE; Key Figures / Belligerents: Abdul Malik ibn Marwan vs Abdullah ibn Zubair; Causes: Consolidation of power; Outcome: Ibn Zubair killed, Umayyads regained full control; Fitna ends
Caliph / Ruler: Yazid I; Period: 680-683 CE; Location / Control: Damascus (Umayyad)
Caliph / Ruler: Muawiyah II; Period: 683-684 CE; Location / Control: Short reign; weak control
Caliph / Ruler: Marwan I; Period: 684-685 CE; Location / Control: Re-established Umayyad leadership
Caliph / Ruler: Abdul Malik ibn Marwan; Period: 685-705 CE; Location / Control: Full Umayyad consolidation
Caliph / Ruler: Abdullah ibn Zubair (Rival Caliph); Period: 680-692 CE; Location / Control: Makkah-based; rival claimant

Event: Ghadir e Khum; Year (Approx.): 632 CE (17 Ramzan on return of Khutba Hajj ul Wida); Location: Ghadir Khum (between Makkah and Madinah); Key Figures Involved: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), Ali (RA), Sahabah; Summary / Significance: Prophet reportedly said: "Whomsoever I am his Mawla (leader), Ali is his Mawla." Highly emphasized in Shia tradition as a declaration of Ali's leadership.

Event: Matter of the Pen (Hadith al-Qirtas); Year (Approx.): Final days of Prophet's life; Location: Prophet's room, Madinah; Key Figures Involved: Prophet (PBUH), Umar (RA), other Sahabah; Summary / Significance: Prophet asked for a pen and paper to write something that would prevent the Ummah from going astray. Umar reportedly said,"The Book of Allah is sufficient for us." Prophet did not write after that.

Event: Event of the Cloak (Hadith al-Kisa); Year (Approx.): Before 10 AH; Location: Prophet's house (Bibi Umme Salma's Hujrah); Key Figures Involved: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), Ali (RA), Fatimah (RA), Hasan (RA), Hussain (RA); Summary / Significance: Prophet took his family under his cloak and said,"These are my Ahl al-Bayt."
Name: Imam Hussain ibn Ali (RA); Side: Pro-Truth; Role: Leader of Prophet's family; Significance: Refused to bow to Yazid's tyranny; central figure of Karbala.
Name: Hazrat Abbas ibn Ali (RA); Side: Hussain's brother; Role: Commander of water mission; Significance: Known for loyalty and bravery; martyred while bringing water.
Name: Ali Akbar ibn Hussain; Side: Hussain's son; Role: Warrior; Significance: Resembled Prophet; martyred in battle.
Name: Ali Asghar; Side: Hussain's infant; Role: Symbol of innocence; Significance: Martyred in father's arms by arrow.
Name: Zainab bint Ali; Side: Hussain's sister; Role: Speaker & moral pillar; Significance: Delivered bold sermons post- Karbala; preserved the message.
Name: Zainul Abideen (Ali ibn Hussain); Side: Son of Hussain; Role: Survived (illness); Significance: Continued Imamship; compiled prayers (Sahifa Sajjadiya).
Name: Hur ibn Yazid al- Riyahi; Side: Switched to Hussain's side; Role: Initially enemy commander; Significance: Repented and joined Hussain before battle. Martyred.
Name: Umar ibn Saad; Side: Yazid's army commander; Role: Led the battle; Significance: Hesitant, yet obeyed orders for power.
Name: Shimr ibn Dhil- Jawshan; Side: Yazid's side; Role: Brutal killer; Significance: Infamously killed Imam Hussain R.A and showed cruelty.
Name: Ubaydullah ibn Ziyad; Side: Governor of Kufa (Yazid's appointee); Role: Political manipulator; Significance: Orchestrated army mobilization and suppression of Kufans.
Name: Yazid ibn Muawiyah; Side: Umayyad Caliph; Role: Central antagonist; Significance: His demand for allegiance triggered the tragedy.
Dynasty Name - Umayyad Caliphate (ةيمأ ونب)
Capital - Damascus (Syria)
Founder - Amir Muawiya I (661-680 AD)
Caliph: Abdul Malik ibn Marwan; Reign: 685-705 AD; Key Highlights: Minted first Islamic coins, Built Dome of the Rock (Palestine/Jerusalem)
Caliph: Al-Walid I; Reign: 705-715 AD; Key Highlights: Empire expanded to Spain, Sindh (by Muhammad bin Qasim), and Central Asia; built Al-Aqsa Mosque (Jerusalem)

Caliph: Umar bin Abdul Aziz (The Pious Caliph); Reign: 717-720 AD; Key Highlights: Known as Umar II,8th Ummayd Caliph, reformist, reduced luxury, promoted justice, invited non-Arabs into Islam with equality (Against discrimination of Persian Muslims)
Later Caliph - (Marwan II)
Causes of Fall - Internal Discontent from Mawalis (Non-Arab Muslims), Corruption and Luxury, Shia Revolts, Abbasid Movement
Dynasty Name - Abbasid Caliphate (سابعلا ونب)
Duration of Rule - 750 AD - 1258 AD (Baghdad-based) Symbolic continuation in Cairo (Mamluks) till 1517 AD
Founded by - Abu al-Abbas Al-Saffah (First Caliph)
Capital City - Initially Kufa, then Baghdad (founded 762 AD by Al-Mansur)
Reason for Rise - Support from Khorasan and non-Arab (Mawali) Muslims - Discontent with Umayyad rule - Propaganda in name of Ahl-e-Bayt (Family of Prophet PBUH)
Major Splits/Breakaway States - Umayyads in Spain (756 AD) - Fatimids in Egypt (909 AD) - Samanids, Ghaznavids, Seljuks ruled under nominal Abbasid suzerainty
Major Invasions - Seljuk Turks (1055 AD): Became protectors of Abbasid caliph - Mongol Invasion (1258 AD): Hulagu Khan sacked Baghdad, Caliph Al-Musta'sim killed
End of Real Abbasid Rule - 1258 AD - Fall of Baghdad by Mongols Last Abbasid Ruler (al-Mustaʿṣim bi-llāh)
Symbolic Continuation - Abbasid caliphs served as religious figureheads under Mamluks in Cairo (1261-1517)
Final End - 1517 AD - Ottoman conquest of Egypt; Abbasid lineage ended
First Abbasid Caliph - Abu al-Abbas Al-Saffah
Abbasid Golden Age ruler - Harun al-Rashid (786-809 AD)
Harun's court was famous for - Luxury, diplomacy, and patronage of scholars
Harun's son, known for scientific advancement - Al-Mamun (813-833 AD)
Bayt-ul-Hikmah (House of Wisdom) established by - Al-Mamun in Baghdad (early 9th century)
Purpose of Bayt-ul-Hikmah - Translation of Greek/Indian works, research in astronomy, medicine, math, philosophy
Decline factors - Weak caliphs, Turkish dominance, court politics, fragmentation
Mongol invasion of Baghdad - 1258 AD by Hulagu Khan - ended central Abbasid power
End of Abbasid symbolic rule - 1517 AD - Ottomans absorbed Caliphate
Scholar/Scientist: Al-Khwarizmi; Major Book / Work: al-Jabr wal-Muqabala; Field / Contribution: Mathematics (Algebra); One-Liner MCQ Tip: Father of Algebra - coined the term Al-Jabr

Scholar/Scientist: Jabir ibn Hayyan (Geber); Major Book / Work: Kitab al-Kimya (Book of Chemistry); Field / Contribution: Chemistry/Alchemy; One-Liner MCQ Tip: Introduced acids, distillation, lab methods
Scholar/Scientist: Ibn Sina (Avicenna); Major Book / Work: Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb (Canon of Medicine); Field / Contribution: Medicine; One-Liner MCQ Tip: Used in Europe till 17th century
Scholar/Scientist: Al-Razi (Rhazes); Major Book / Work: Kitab al-Hawi (Comprehensive Book); Field / Contribution: Medicine; One-Liner MCQ Tip: Encyclopedic medical reference
